Renard, B., Garreta, V., and Lang, M. (2006), 
“An application of Bayesian analysis and Markov chain Monte Carlo methods to the estimation of a regional trend in annual maxima,” 
Water Resources Research, 
42, 
2005WR004591.  https://doi.org/10.1029/2005WR004591.

We can use Bayesian inference in order to assess the suitability of a proposed model for a dynamic system. 
$$
\begin{aligned}
P(M_j|X) &= \frac{P(X|M_j)\pi(M_j)}{\sum_{i=1}^{q}P(M_i|X)\pi(M_i)}
\end{aligned}
$$
Where $M_k$ is the kth proposed model, q is the number of models we propose, and $\pi(M_k)$ is the probability of using model $M_k$ within a Markov chain comprised of porposed models.
$P(X|M) = \int P(X,\theta|M)d\theta$ is extremely difficult to solve numerically for high dimensions.  So, we approximate $P(X|M)$ using MCMC methods and reassess suitability using Bayes factors where the Bayes factor comparing model i and model j is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
B_{i,j} = \frac{P(X|M_i)}{P(X|M_j)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Where the usage of model $M_i$ is supported by high values of $B_{i,j}$.

It is important to note that $M_i$ and $M_j$ are not neccessarily of different distributions, but instead different parameters chosen.  In this application, the Markov chain is comprised of iteratively selecting different parameters (denoted as $\theta^\tau$ where $\tau$ is the $\tau$th vector of parameters generated).
